meta.tldr: This 4.1.9 release for Cline focuses on significant bug fixes and UI refinements, particularly for users of the SDK bundle. A key visual improvement is the use of the editor's foreground color for diff block text, ensuring legibility across various themes, and a refreshed interface with the Inter and Geist Mono fonts. Critical fixes include preventing the discarding of successfully refreshed Cline tokens, which previously caused failed requests after idle periods, and addressing issues with legacy-task migration telemetry to ensure accurate reporting. For SDK bundle users, the Claude Code provider is now fully functional for agentic work, correctly utilizing native tools, anchoring sessions to workspace directories, and loading user settings. The release also rectifies issues with truncated tool-call JSON being silently 'repaired' into incorrect arguments, and strict providers rejecting turns with empty text parts in messages. Furthermore, a mid-turn crash with streamed tool calls via LiteLLM's Anthropic passthrough has been resolved, and token counting for cached conversations is now accurate, preventing inflated per-task totals. These updates collectively enhance the stability, usability, and accuracy of Cline, especially for developers leveraging the SDK bundle. Users are encouraged to upgrade to benefit from these crucial fixes and UI improvements, particularly if experiencing issues with token refreshing, agentic workflows with Claude Code, or inaccurate token usage reporting.

breaking_changes.title: Remove Foreground Terminal Mode
breaking_changes.description: Foreground terminal mode has been removed. All task command execution now defaults to background mode, removing the VS Code integrated terminal dependency and related settings UI.
breaking_changes.migration: No migration is required. All task commands will now execute in the background.

breaking_changes.title: Removal of Model-Initiated Plan-to-Act Switching
breaking_changes.description: The model will no longer automatically switch from plan mode to act mode. Switching out of plan mode is now exclusively user-driven.
breaking_changes.migration: Users must now explicitly trigger the switch from plan mode to act mode. The model will no longer make this decision mid-turn.

breaking_changes.title: Hard-blocking File-Editing Shell Commands in Plan Mode
breaking_changes.description: File-editing shell commands are now hard-blocked in plan mode. This includes file manipulation, in-place editors, redirection to files, mutating git subcommands, and package installs. Read-only investigation commands are still permitted.
affected: Shell command execution in plan mode
breaking_changes.migration: Users must switch out of plan mode to execute any shell commands that modify files or system state. Attempting to run such commands in plan mode will result in refusal.

breaking_changes.title: Model-initiated plan-to-act switching removed
breaking_changes.description: Switching out of plan mode is now driven by the user, not by the model deciding mid-turn. This means the model will no longer automatically transition from planning to acting.
breaking_changes.migration: Users will now need to explicitly drive the transition from plan mode to act mode. The model will no longer initiate this switch.

breaking_changes.title: Removal of Yolo Mode Toggle
breaking_changes.description: The 'Yolo Mode' toggle has been removed as it was a cosmetic feature with no functional impact on the approval path. The auto-approve menu is now the sole control for unattended runs.
affected: Users who relied on the 'Yolo Mode' toggle for visual confirmation of unattended runs.
breaking_changes.migration: Existing configurations that had 'Yolo Mode' or 'auto-approve-all' turned on will be automatically migrated to auto-approve every action, ensuring continued unattended operation. No manual migration steps are required, but users should now use the auto-approve menu for all unattended run configurations.
